extracted.intended_audience: small business applicants preparing NIH/NIAID SBIR Phase II (PHS) grant applications in biomedical research
extracted.subtask_description: Preparation and submission of a NIH/NIAID SBIR Phase II (PHS) grant application including required forms, research plan sections, facilities/equipment descriptions, biosafety and animal-use documentation, budgets, and letters of support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow FOA/application format instructions
rubrics_metrics.description: Always follow your funding opportunity's instructions for application format. Although this application demonstrates good grantsmanship, time has passed since the grantee applied. The samples may not reflect the latest format or rules. NIAID posts new samples periodically: https://www.niaid.nih.gov/grants-contracts/sample-applications
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adhere exactly to the Funding Opportunity Announcement (FOA) and agency-specific instructions; use current samples and guidance from the institute; do not assume an older sample matches current requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complete SF 424 (R&R) cover and required form fields
rubrics_metrics.description: Application must include SF 424 (R&R) information: type of submission, federal identifier, applicant organization DUNS/EIN, type of applicant, project title, proposed start and end dates, PD/PI contact information, authorized representative signature and certifications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide all required identifiers and contact data (DUNS, EIN, addresses, phone/email), mark application type (new/resubmission/etc.), declare other-agency submissions, and obtain signature of authorized representative certifying statements/assurances.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Summary/Abstract required
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach a Project Summary/Abstract describing the proposal (file indicated: ABSTRACT ... vaccinePhaseIIFINAL.pdf).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Summarize significance, objectives, approach, and expected outcomes concisely in the abstract as part of the application package.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project Narrative (Public Health Relevance Statement)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include a Project Narrative that states the public health relevance (NARRATIVE (PUBLIC HEALTH RELEVANCE STATEMENT)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly describe why the project matters for public health (burden, unmet need, urgency) in plain-language accessible to non-specialists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan structure and required sections
rubrics_metrics.description: The Research Plan must include Specific Aims, Research Strategy, Vertebrate Animals, Bibliography & References Cited, Letters of Support, and Appendix (see Table of Contents referencing these sections).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organize the research plan into the standard NIH sections and include the indicated attachments (e.g., references, letters, appendix) as separate files.

rubrics_metrics.name: Facilities & Other Resources description
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide Facilities & Other Resources: detailed descriptions of office and laboratory space, animal facilities (BSL level), agreements with host institutions, square footage, available computers and network access, and proximity to core centers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate adequacy of physical space and institutional support, list inter-institutional agreements, and describe how facilities will support the proposed research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equipment listing and core facility access
rubrics_metrics.description: List all available equipment in applicant laboratories and core facilities (e.g., QPCR, flow cytometers, confocal microscopes, lyophilizers, particle analyzers), including university core resources available by agreement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide an inventory of key instruments and note formal access agreements or collaborations that guarantee use of specialized equipment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Budget Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Research & Related Budget pages for each year, cumulative budget, and a Budget Justification attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide year-by-year direct costs, indicate consortium F&A exclusions where relevant, and justify personnel, supplies, subcontractor costs, and other budget line items in the justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: SBIR/STTR-specific attachments (Commercialization Plan, Prior SBIR awards)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide SBIR/STTR Information and a Commercialization Plan; include documentation of prior SBIR Phase II awards where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe market potential, commercialization strategy, milestones, and prior SBIR history to demonstrate commercial feasibility and company progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biographical sketches and current & pending support for key personnel
rubrics_metrics.description: Attach biographical sketches (biosketch) and Current & Pending Support documents for the PD/PI and senior/key personnel.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include education/training, personal statement, positions/honors, selected contributions, and full disclosure of other active or pending support that could affect project commitment or overlap.

rubrics_metrics.name: Human Subjects involvement declaration and IRB status
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether human subjects are involved; if yes, declare whether the project is exempt, provide exemption number or indicate IRB review pending and IRB approval date as applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer the human subjects questions on the application and provide IRB documentation or exemption justification; do not leave fields ambiguous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals declaration and IACUC status
rubrics_metrics.description: Indicate whether vertebrate animals are used; if yes, state whether IACUC review is pending or provide the IACUC approval date and Animal Welfare Assurance Number.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide full IACUC documentation, assurance numbers, and any required animal-use protocols or descriptions of animal procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Occupational Health Monitoring Program enrollment for animal work
rubrics_metrics.description: Personnel in contact with research animals or unfixed tissues must enroll in the Occupational Health Monitoring Program (OHMP) at SUNY at Buffalo; the program is mandatory and costs are covered by the University.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all animal-handling personnel complete OHMP questionnaire and health information review; retain evidence of enrollment and follow OHMP recommendations (vaccinations, etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: Register hazardous agents with University Biosafety Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: All researchers using potentially hazardous agents (infectious agents, toxic chemicals, recombinant DNA) must inform the University Biosafety Committee by registering their research program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide written hazard descriptions (MSDS), register projects with biosafety oversight, and ensure institutional biosafety review is completed prior to initiating work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal Investigator responsibilities for hazard communication and training
rubrics_metrics.description: The Principal Investigator is responsible to provide appropriate information on hazardous materials to all who may be exposed, including (a) written hazard descriptions (MSDS); (b) hazard-specific and documented training of personnel; and (c) posting of appropriate standardized signage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document training records, make MSDS accessible, and post standardized signs on holding rooms and labs before starting projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: BSL-2 facility use and PPE for Neisseria gonorrhoeae work
rubrics_metrics.description: All work with Neisseria gonorrhoeae will be conducted in the BSL Level 2 Facility. Standard entry, gowning, and personal hygiene procedures of BSL2 will be followed. NIOSH N95 face masks and safety glasses will be worn in animal holding rooms and during cage changes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with BSL-2 containment practices and require appropriate PPE for staff when handling organisms or animals; include these safeguards in the application and SOPs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decontamination and removal procedures from BSL2
rubrics_metrics.description: All equipment and supplies must be autoclaved or disinfected with alcohol or 10% bleach prior to removal from BSL2. Cages & bedding will be autoclaved prior to removal; after autoclaving, bedding will be discarded into Red Biohazard bags and disposed as Certified Medical Waste.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Describe validated decontamination procedures, autoclave logs, and certified medical waste disposal arrangements in application facilities documents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Carcass handling: treat as infectious and incinerate
rubrics_metrics.description: Carcasses must be treated as infectious and incinerated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include carcass handling and disposal plans consistent with institutional and regulatory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exposure incident notification and medical follow-up procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: If a contaminated needle-stick or mucous membrane exposure occurs, follow SOP #3.F.1: (A) Notify your supervisor, (B) Call ECMC 898-4153 and ask to see a doctor, (C) Inform workers compensation at 645-5000 X1025, (D) After-hours proceed to ECMC and explain you are enrolled in OHMP, (E) Medical attention should be sought within 24 hours of the exposure or injury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide clear, stepwise exposure response SOPs in facility documentation and ensure workers know after-hours procedures and contact numbers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for Neisseria gonorrhoeae safety precautions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Comparative Medicine Laboratory Animal Facilities STANDARD OPERATING PROCEDURE for NEISSERIA GONORRHOEAE SAFETY PRECAUTIONS must be followed and is included as an attachment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attach organism-specific SOPs outlining purpose, scope, and procedural safeguards; ensure SOPs are complete and institutionally approved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Animal facility accreditation and compliance statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Research animal facilities are accredited by AAALAC and comply with all applicable Federal and State laws and guidelines. The program provides procurement, routine animal care, health surveillance, and veterinary support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document AAALAC accreditation, OLAW/USDA registrations, and availability of veterinary support and services in the facilities description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core facility agreements and collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: List inter-institutional agreements allowing access to core instrumentation (e.g., Confocal Microscopy and Flow Cytometry core at Witebsky Center), and name facility directors/administrators who will assist (e.g., Dr. Wade J. Sigurdson, Dr. Ray Kelleher).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include letters or agreement documents confirming access, usage terms, and any associated fees or scheduling arrangements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Letters of Support must document resource and collaboration commitments
rubrics_metrics.description: Include Letters of Support from collaborators and service providers describing specific commitments (e.g., provision of clinical isolates, transformation of strains, fee-for-service support for toxicology, regulatory consultation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Letters should specify what will be provided, quantities/timelines (e.g., up to 30 clinical isolates, transforming up to 6 strains), and any conditions or costs; they substantiate feasibility and partnerships.

rubrics_metrics.name: FOIA and confidentiality considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: When NIH responds to FOIA requests for grant applications and summary statements, the material will be subject to FOIA exemptions and include substantial redactions. NIH must protect all confidential commercial or financial information, reviewer comments and deliberations, and personal privacy information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mark proprietary sections appropriately and be aware that submitted applications may be released with redactions under FOIA; do not include unnecessary proprietary detail in public sections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 508 accessibility conformance note
rubrics_metrics.description: Note on Section 508 Conformance and Accessibility: sample was reformatted to improve accessibility for people with disabilities and users of assistive technology; contact provided if trouble accessing content.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure submitted documents meet accessibility standards or provide accessible alternatives as required; include contact information for accessibility issues.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declare proprietary/privileged information and environmental impact
rubrics_metrics.description: The application must state whether proprietary/privileged information is included and whether the project has actual or potential environmental impact; if environmental impact exists, indicate if an exemption, environmental assessment (EA), or environmental impact statement (EIS) has been performed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Answer these administrative questions clearly and, if environmental review is needed, provide the necessary documentation or explanations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Project performance site details required
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide project/performance site locations, organization names, DUNS numbers, and congressional district(s) for each site.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: List primary and additional performance sites with full addresses and associated congressional districts; ensure consistency with institutional agreements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorized representative certification and signature
rubrics_metrics.description: By signing the application, the authorized representative certifies the statements in the list of certifications and assurances and agrees to comply with resulting terms; false statements may result in penalties (U.S. Code, Title 18, Section 1001).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure the authorized official signs and dates the application and that institutional authorities have reviewed and approved all commitments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attach supporting documents (e.g., Facilities, Equipment, References) as separate files
rubrics_metrics.description: The Table of Contents lists attachments and file names: Project Summary/Abstract, Project Narrative, Bibliography & References Cited, Facilities & Other Resources, Equipment, etc., each as separate uploaded files.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Upload each supporting document as a distinct file with meaningful filenames and correct MIME types; follow FOA file-size and format restrictions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide detailed SOPs for animal housing and husbandry linked to organism risk
rubrics_metrics.description: The SOP outlines scope, occupational risk (organism infectious exclusively to humans), risk characteristics (not transmissible mouse-to-mouse, susceptible to disinfectants), and procedural controls (autoclaving, PPE, monitoring).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain animal housing arrangements, sanitation, cage-change procedures, and any organism-specific constraints and how they affect experimental design.

rubrics_metrics.name: List institutional and external service providers with commitments (e.g., contract research organizations, regulatory consultants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Letters describe commitments from entities such as Comparative Biosciences, Inc. (preclinical toxicology services) and Regulatory Professionals, Inc. (regulatory strategy and IND/type C meeting preparation).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include scope, capabilities, accreditations (GLP, OLAW, AAALAC), and specific services to be provided, to support the feasibility and regulatory path.
